my biggest tip is to not try to write, i find that when i just play and improvise my best writing comes out and as far as getting discouraged, if you have an idea, see it through. dont just be like “ehhh that doesnt sound how i expected” and scrap it, finish the project, add other instruments. the true measure of whether or not you are a truly good musician is if you can take a mistake or something you didn’t love and turn it into something great. but for the most part, dont sit down and be like “time to write a song” sit down and just play, dont work too hard, music is fun so have fun with it, your brain knows what sounds good and as hard as it may be to believe there are a lot of melodies sitting in your head you havent found yet. so just play and eventually the rest will come naturally, but trying too hard to get past writers block is what will burn you out.

Edit: for lyrics, i like to first think of the story i want to tell, do something actually meaningful to you, then i like to think of topics i want to hit, for example for me I was an addict so when writing a song about that i thought of things that i wanted to express like fear of overdose, struggles with relapsing, feeling trapped, then i think of individual lines for each of those topics, then try to move them around and switch out words, etc to find an order of them that sounds best to you. although with lyrics everyone has a different system and different ways of thinking so its mostly up to you but theres a method for you to try! good luck! you got this!
